issues.reason: Propositional attitudes says "Parse P as usual (classes, roles, tense), then seal it", and its own example seals (Past sk_leave_1) for "Nadia believes Tom left", so the past-tense "he thought" must carry (Past sk_think_1) inside the seal.
Dropping "perhaps" makes the sealed proposition record an unhedged second venue, asserting more of what Rork thought than the text states.

Two Location atoms on one appeal event say one appealing happened in both courts, which is false of "appeal the ruling in state court and perhaps in U.S. District Court"; Coordination & plurals makes coordination distributive by default, replicating the predication once per conjunct.

gaps_confirmed: "perhaps" has no listed epistemic operator — the status table names only might / probably / must (note: status atoms themselves do sit inside a seal, as the parse's own (Future sk_ask_1) shows, so the seal is not the obstacle)
coordinated PP adjuncts on one event — distributive replication is spelled out only for coordinated argument NPs and for clauses / VPs
new_gaps: sequence-of-tense in a doubly embedded report ("said he thought") — nothing states whether the inner past is an independent past or backshift agreement with the matrix, so whether (Past sk_think_1) is a claim about time or about morphology is undecided
repair_summary: Added (Past sk_think_1) inside the say event's sealed Theme. Split the single appeal into sk_appeal_1 (state_court) and sk_appeal_2 (us_district_court), each a Theme of sk_ask_1 with its own class, Agent rork and Theme sk_ruling_1, so no one event is located in two courts. Tagged the second with (Might sk_appeal_2) to carry "perhaps".
notes: Might is used for "perhaps" as the epistemic-possibility sense of the same operator family, per "drop the same surface word's sense into the right operator"; the confidence-0.9 convention cannot apply because conjuncts inside a seal carry no TV of their own.
